cards.explanation: The answer is seven. Zechariah sees "a solid gold lampstand, with a bowl at the top and seven lamps on it, with seven spouts to the lamps." (Zechariah 4:2) That's a lot of lamps on one stand, and every one has its own spout. Solid gold too, friends, which is a lot nicer than anything in the junk drawer I used to live in.

The answer is olive trees. Zechariah says, "There are also two olive trees beside it, one on the right side of the bowl and the other on its left." (Zechariah 4:3) One tree on each side of the bowl, standing there like two guards at the oven door. Hold onto those trees, bakers, because Zechariah is going to ask about them.

The answer is True. The angel asks, "Do you not know what they are?" and Zechariah answers, "No, my lord…" (Zechariah 4:5) He just says it plain. No bluffing, no nodding along. I have to respect a man who admits he doesn't know.

The answer is by the LORD's Spirit. The word says, "Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of Hosts." (Zechariah 4:6) The LORD is the one speaking, so "My Spirit" means His Spirit. Zerubbabel gets the message straight from the LORD.

The answer is plain. The word says, "Before Zerubbabel you will become a plain." (Zechariah 4:7) A great mountain gets flattened right out. I've rolled out some stubborn dough in my day, friends, but that's a whole other level of flat.

The answer is Zerubbabel. The word says, "Then he will bring forth the capstone accompanied by shouts of ‘Grace, grace to it!’…" (Zechariah 4:7) The "he" is the same Zerubbabel the word was just speaking to. Shouting "Grace, grace" over a capstone sounds like my kind of party.

The answer is False. The word says, "The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will complete it." (Zechariah 4:9) His hands do both jobs, start and finish. The text doesn't hand the job off to anyone else.

The answer is rejoice. "…these seven eyes of the LORD, which scan the whole earth, will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel." (Zechariah 4:10) A plumb line is a builder's tool, so that's a happy sight for the eyes. I like that picture of eyes rejoicing over a plumb line, friends.

The answer is oil. Zechariah asks about "…the two gold pipes from which the golden oil pours?" (Zechariah 4:12) Golden oil pouring out of gold pipes, which is a pretty fancy setup. Olive trees and oil go together, so I think that fits.

The answer is two anointed ones standing beside the Lord. The angel says, "These are the two anointed ones who are standing beside the Lord of all the earth." (Zechariah 4:14) It took him a couple of tries, but Zechariah finally gets his answer. The angel doesn't name the two, so I won't either.
